messages:
Sara L: Heads-up: forecasting for Q4 surge — need to validate admission-control thresholds for p95=250ms, p99=900ms across hosted and dedicated pools. Current plan: 20% headroom. Any quick sanity checks?

Ajay P: Do we have arrival rate profile? peak qps per shard?

Sara L: Quick numbers: baseline 220 qps across us-west cluster, expected seasonal spike +60% for Black Friday window -> ~352 qps. Avg tokens/request unchanged.

Marcos G: If we approximate as M/M/c with service time ~120ms per request on p4d-like GPU => µ ≈ 8.33 req/s per GPU. Naive calc: servers ≈ λ/(µ * util_target). With util_target=0.65 -> 352/(8.33*0.65) ≈ 65 GPUs.

Olivia Ops: That looks large. Are we accounting for batching / prefix cache? Batching can increase effective µ.

Marcos G: Yes — with batching we see µ_effective ≈ 12 req/s for this workload -> GPUs ≈ 352/(12*0.65) ≈ 45.

Kai S: Note p99 tail is sensitive to util. Even if p95 ok, p99 will explode as util->1. Recommend admission control: queue length limit + token-bucket rejects. Proposal: Q_max=50, soft reject when p95>280ms, hard reject when p99>900ms.

Ajay P: Can we make it adaptive? Softly throttle when p95 crosses threshold, tighten at higher percentiles, and failover to dedicated pool when hosted util > 0.8.

Sara L: Ops ask for GPU-hour budget for BF window: 72h, baseline 45 GPUs + 30% burst => peak ~58 GPUs. Rough GPUh = 58 * 72 = 4176 GPUh. Add 15% buffer -> ~4803 GPUh. Does that match your calc?

Olivia Ops: Yes. At $3.5/GPUh -> ~$16.8k raw for compute. We should model reserved discounts and egress.

Marcos G: Also account for cold starts & churn. Recommend a 6h canary with stricter admission (Q_max=25) to validate latency before pushing full capacity.

deploy-bot: deploy started: admission-control/soft-throttle v1 -> staging at 1768880036

Kai S: Quick config snippet for ops team:
```
Q_MAX=50
SOFT_P95_TRIGGER_MS=280
HARD_P99_TRIGGER_MS=900
ROUTE_TO_DEDICATED_UTIL=0.8
```

Kai S: Also add alerts: queue_length > 40 for 1m, tail_latency_p99 > 700ms for 2m, hosted_util > 0.75.

Ajay P: I'll run a small queuing sim and post results here. Expected output: p95 and p99 vs util curves, plus GPUh estimate.

Sara L: Thanks — please @Ajay P when done. We need numbers for the forecast doc to present to finance. :thumbsup:

Ajay P: Sim summary posted: arrival peak 352 qps, with batching µ_eff=12 and Q_max=50 we get p95 ~ 260ms, p99 ~ 820ms, GPU hours ~4700 including buffer. Admission hits ~4% of requests at peak.

Sara L: That looks acceptable. We'll bake into the forecast and recommend the admission policy + dedicated failover. TY everyone.
